messages:
jin: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection rollout + new batching heuristic, we're seeing intermittent 10-30s stalls on multi-node TP inference (8-node, TP=2). Happened 3x in the last 2 hours.

maya: Ugh. Any pattern? cold start vs steady-state? specific seq len?

jin: Appears during steady-state when many simultaneous short requests hit KV cache. Not at startup. Sequence lengths ~512 mostly.

sam: Do we have NCCL timeouts or python hangs? logs?

jin: Logs show barrier wait spikes. No python traceback, worker processes are alive. Example from node-4: 

```
2026-11-02T14:02:11Z WARN barrier: wait_for_barrier exceeded 15000ms
2026-11-02T14:02:11Z INFO comm: allreduce start id=0x7f
2026-11-02T14:02:21Z INFO comm: allreduce complete id=0x7f (node-4 delayed)
```

jon: infra-bot: canary rollout of kernel-selector v2 complete at 13:40 UTC (5% traffic)

maya: That barrier line smells like imbalance/straggler on one rank. Could be a kernel path that becomes much slower for short sequences. Any perf profiles?

jin: I ran a quick nvprof on a repro pod. Not a single huge kernel — instead long tail of many small kernels plus extra memcpy calls. Raw stack hints at fallback matmul kernel for odd tensor shapes.

ryan: Could the batching heuristic be creating micro-batches that change memory alignment and trigger fallback kernels? We recently changed to pack by token count + priority ordering.

sam: Also check KV cache sharding across TP ranks. If one rank gets more cache hits, it might run more KV ops and block the all-reduce start. Are KV ops synchronous on the same stream?

jin: Good call. I instrumented streams: KV writes happen on stream 0 (same as compute) before triggering comm on stream 1. But on the slow rank we see extra stream0->stream1 syncs.

maya: Can you grab a timeline from nsight or CUPTI? Even a simple cudaEvent timeline could show stream stalls.

jin: I'm collecting CUPTI traces now. Meanwhile I added envs for next run: 
```
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
TORCH_DISTRIBUTED_DEBUG=INFO
REDWOOD_RUNTIME_TRACE=kv,comm,kernel
```

sam: Also try forcing the previously known-good kernel selector (rollback) on one canary cluster to compare. If stalls go away that's telling.

infra-bot: rolled rollback to kernel-selector v1 on canary-2 at 14:10 UTC (10% traffic)

ryan: If v1 fixes it, then it's kernel selection. If not, it's likely batching->KV imbalance. We should also test with KV ops moved to a dedicated stream to avoid implicit sync.

jin: Repro run on canary-2 (v1) for 20 min — no stalls so far. On v2 another run hit a 22s barrier wait.

maya: That's strong signal for kernel selector change. We should capture a perf diff: kernel times, memcpy counts, and all-reduce start latency distribution per rank.

sam: Can we also test with quantization variant? v2 picks a different GEMM kernel for q4; maybe it chosen a non-vectorized fallback for odd widths.

jin: Good idea. I'll run three matrix: v1, v2, v2+dedicated-kv-stream, and collect per-rank metrics (kernel time histogram, memcpy bytes, barrier latencies).

ryan: Add a small synthetic where we force skewed KV distribution to see sensitivity. If imbalance triggers stalls, we can prioritize KV sharding or async KV flush.

oncall: tagging for oncall — if this affects production SLA, escalate. What's current impact?

jin: Production saw 4 user-visible slow requests in the last 2 hours. Not critical yet but reproducible in canary.

maya: Action items: 
- jin: run the 3-matrix experiments and upload traces (CUPTI + nvprof) 
- sam: instrument kernel-selector telemetry to log chosen kernel id + input shape for suspicious cases 
- ryan: prototype moving KV ops to separate stream and test on v2
- maya: prepare rollback plan for v2 fully if canary shows continued regressions

sam: small note — when you upload traces include mapping from job-id -> node IP -> rank so we can correlate rank 4 slowdowns.

jin: will do. starting experiment now, ETA 30m. uploading timeline to S3: s3://redwood-perf/1823456789/jin-timelines/

maya: thanks. If you hit an easy mitigation (dedicated kv stream or forcing v1 kernel for short seq) we can turn on auto-fallback in the runtime quickly.

jin: If fallback helps I'll open a patch and a canary rollback PR. Will post results in this thread.

infra-bot: note — created perf-issue #INF-4312 for tracking

ryan: pro-tip: add cudaProfilerInitialize + cudaProfilerStart in the repro harness to avoid missing early kernels in CUPTI traces.

jin: got it, thanks. uploading first set of traces now.

sam: awesome. ping when traces uploaded and I'll start parsing kernel id -> time.

jin: uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1823456789/jin-timelines/v1_trace.zip and v2_trace.zip and v2_kvstream_trace.zip

maya: starting triage. earliest observation: v2 has 3x memcpy calls per step on slow rank vs v1. That could explain the tail.

sam: looks like kernel-selector picked 'gemm_fallback_odd' for shape (64,37) on v2. v1 used 'gemm_fast_padded' which fused memcpy.

maya: OK that's a clear regression. Plan: revert selector rule that picks fallback for odd widths, and add a padding fast-path in v2 to avoid fallback.

jin: filed PR to pin kernel-selector config on canary and add padding patch for v2 (PR: https://git.redwood/co/repo/pulls/774)

oncall: keep monitoring. escalate if user-impact grows.

maya: great work. once patch passes canary we'll schedule a full rollback and run broader perf tests for other seq lengths.

jin: closing loop later with final metrics. thanks team :thumbsup:
